proposals.before: Yelü Chucai, whose courtesy name was Jinqing, was a great-great-grandson in the eighth generation of Yelü Tuyu, the Liao Prince of Dongdan.
proposals.after: Yelü Chucai, whose courtesy name was Jinqing, was an eighth-generation descendant of Yelü Tuyu, the Liao Prince of Dongdan.
proposals.reason: 八世孫 means eighth-generation descendant; 'great-great-grandson in the eighth generation' conflates and misstates the generation distance.

proposals.before: On the day the war banners were consecrated, snow piled three feet deep; when the emperor was troubled by the omen, Chucai said, "Yin force manifesting in midsummer is a sign that the enemy will be overcome."
proposals.after: On the day the war banners were consecrated, rain and snow piled three feet deep; when the emperor was troubled by the omen, Chucai said, "Yin force manifesting in midsummer is a sign that the enemy will be overcome."
proposals.reason: Chinese 雨雪三尺 denotes rain and snow together; the idiomatic rendering drops rain and says only snow.

proposals.before: Xiandebo, nursing an old grudge, hated him all the more and slandered him to a imperial prince: "The Yelü director of the Secretariat fills his office with kin and cronies; he must be disloyal—memorialize for his execution."
proposals.after: Xiandebo, nursing an old grudge, hated him all the more and slandered him to an imperial prince: "The Yelü director of the Secretariat fills his office with kin and cronies; he must be disloyal—memorialize for his execution."
proposals.reason: Grammatical error: English requires "an" before the vowel sound in "imperial".

proposals.before: Thereupon he memorialized to establish tax-collection commissioners for the ten circuits including Yanjing; all chief and deputy posts were filled with scholar-officials such as Chen Shike and Zhao Fang, all men of generous and mature character, the finest selection in the realm, and assistants were all drawn from former personnel of the provincial departments.
proposals.after: Thereupon he memorialized to establish tax-collection commissioners for the ten circuits including Yanjing; all chief and deputy posts were filled with scholar-officials such as Chen Shike and Zhao Fang, all men of generous and mature character, the finest selection in the realm, and assistants were all drawn from former personnel of the Secretariat and ministries.
proposals.reason: 省部 denotes the central Secretariat and ministries, not provincial departments; the idiomatic already renders this as former central-government staff.

proposals.before: He ordered Liu Zhong, tax commissioner of Xuanede, to hold examinations in every commandery in three fields—classics, rhapsodies, and policy essays. Captured scholars enslaved were also to sit the exam; masters who hid them were put to death.
proposals.after: He ordered Liu Zhong, tax commissioner of Xuande, to hold examinations in every commandery in three fields—classics, rhapsodies, and policy essays. Captured scholars enslaved were also to sit the exam; masters who hid them were put to death.
proposals.reason: Chinese 宣德州 is Xuande Prefecture; idiomatic English misspells it as Xuanede.

proposals.before: Thereupon he ordered Liu Zhong, tax commissioner of Xuanede Prefecture, to conduct examinations in each commandery, divided into three categories—classics, rhapsodies, and discourses; Confucian scholars taken captive as slaves were also ordered to sit the examination, and masters who concealed them and did not send them were to die.
proposals.after: Thereupon he ordered Liu Zhong, tax commissioner of Xuande Prefecture, to conduct examinations in each commandery, divided into three categories—classics, rhapsodies, and discourses; Confucian scholars taken captive as slaves were also ordered to sit the examination, and masters who concealed them and did not send them were to die.
proposals.reason: Chinese 宣德州 is Xuande Prefecture; literal English misspells it as Xuanede Prefecture.

proposals.before: He answered, "Even a father teaching his sons does not wish them to fall into wickedness.
proposals.after: He answered, "Even a lord and father teaching his ministers and sons does not wish them to fall into wickedness.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English drops 君 and 臣 from 君父教臣子, reducing the lord/father and minister/son parallel.

proposals.before: The palace favorite again accused Chucai of violating regulations; the Emperor was angry and imprisoned Chucai;
proposals.after: The palace favorite again accused Chucai of violating regulations; the Emperor was angry and had Chucai bound;
proposals.reason: 系 means binding/fettering here, matching the following refusal to be unbound; imprisoned overstates it.

proposals.before: The emperor loved wine and drank daily with his ministers; Chucai remonstrated repeatedly in vain, then brought a wine trough with an iron spout and said, "Ferment can rot iron—what will it do to the five organs!"
proposals.after: The emperor loved wine and drank daily with his ministers; Chucai remonstrated repeatedly in vain, then brought a wine trough with an iron spout and said, "Yeast can corrode things; if even iron is thus, how much more the five organs!"
proposals.reason: Chinese 曲蘗能腐物，鐵尚如此 is an a fortiori from corroded iron to the viscera, not a direct claim that ferment rots iron alone.

proposals.before: Still asleep, he was about to rebuke whoever disturbed him when he opened his eyes and saw the emperor; he started up in alarm to apologize. The emperor said, "Drinking alone—will you not share the pleasure with me?"
proposals.after: Chucai was still in deep sleep and had not awakened; he was just angry at being disturbed when he suddenly opened his eyes, realized the emperor had come, and started up in alarm to apologize. The emperor said, "You have wine and get drunk alone—will you not share the pleasure with me?"
proposals.reason: Idiomatic omits 楚材熟睡未醒 and softens 有酒獨醉 relative to the Chinese.

proposals.before: The emperor reproached Chucai: "You said Confucian teaching could govern the realm and that scholars were good men—why then do we have men like these?"
proposals.after: The emperor reproached Chucai: "You said Confucius's teaching could govern the realm and that Confucians are good men—why then do we have men like these?"
proposals.reason: Idiomatic renders 孔子之教 as generic "Confucian teaching" and 儒者 as "scholars", losing the named 孔子 and the Confucian class noun present in the Chinese and literal.

proposals.before: In the first year of Zhishun he was posthumously given the title Merit-holder Who Deliberates on State Regulation with Vigorous Brilliance and Assists the Mandate, Grand Preceptor, and Upper Pillar of the State, enfeoffed posthumously as Prince of Guangning, with the temple name Wenzheng.
proposals.after: In the first year of Zhishun he was posthumously given the title Merit-holder Who Deliberates on State Regulation with Vigorous Brilliance and Assists the Mandate, Grand Preceptor, and Upper Pillar of the State, enfeoffed posthumously as Prince of Guangning, with the posthumous name Wenzheng.
proposals.reason: 諡 denotes a posthumous name, not a temple name (廟號).

proposals.before: In the first year of Zhishun he was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor and Upper Pillar of the State, enfeoffed as Prince of Guangning, with the posthumous name Wenzheng.
proposals.after: In the first year of Zhishun he was posthumously honored as Merit-holder Who Deliberates on State Regulation with Vigorous Brilliance and Assists the Mandate, Grand Preceptor, and Upper Pillar of the State, enfeoffed as Prince of Guangning, with the posthumous name Wenzheng.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English omits the conferred merit title 經國議制寅亮佐運功臣 present in the Chinese.

proposals.after: His sons were Xuan and Zhu.
proposals.reason: 鉉 is Xuàn (Xuan), not Xian.

proposals.before: He died and was posthumously made Grand Commandant, enfeoffed as Duke of Wei, with the temple name Zhongwu.
proposals.after: He died and was posthumously made Grand Commandant, enfeoffed as Duke of Wei, with the posthumous name Zhongwu.
proposals.reason: 諡 denotes a posthumous name, not a temple name (廟號).

proposals.before: At the time the various army commanders were overbearing and extravagant, harming the people; the thousand-household chief Guo was especially so, killing a man's husband and seizing his wife; Weizhong executed him as a warning, and Guanzhong was solemnly ordered.
proposals.after: At the time the various army commanders were overbearing and extravagant, harming the people; the thousand-household chief Guo was especially so, killing a man and seizing his wife; Weizhong executed him as a warning, and Guanzhong was solemnly ordered.
proposals.reason: Literal English mistranslates 殺人之夫 as "a man's husband"; it means killing a (woman's) husband and seizing his wife.

proposals.before: In the second year of Zhongtong he was posthumously given the temple name Duke Zhongsu.
proposals.after: In the second year of Zhongtong he was posthumously given the posthumous name Duke Zhongsu.
proposals.reason: 諡 is a posthumous name, not a temple name; the literal English mislabels 忠肅公.

proposals.before: Earlier, when Kublai campaigned against Song at Bian, Nanhe said, "Li Tan has received great favor from the state and holds a region on his own, yet his followers are treacherous—rebellion is only a matter of time."
proposals.after: Earlier, when Kublai campaigned against Song at Bian, Nanhe said, "Li Tan has received great favor from the state and holds a region on his own, yet the man is full of deceit—rebellion is only a matter of time."
proposals.reason: 其人多詐 refers to Li Tan's own deceitful character, not that "his followers" are treacherous.

decisions.reason: 八世孫 means an eighth-generation descendant; 'great-great-grandson in the eighth generation' wrongly conflates degrees of descent with generation count.

In the classical construction 雨雪, 雨 is the verb 'to fall' and 雪 is its subject: snow fell to a depth of three feet. The existing English preserves the event; adding rain would introduce a second kind of precipitation absent from the Chinese.
'a imperial prince' is ungrammatical; English requires 'an' before the vowel onset of imperial.
省部 means the central Secretariat and ministries, not provincial departments; the proposed correction matches the Chinese and the idiomatic field.
宣德州 is Xuande Prefecture; 'Xuanede' is a misspelling of the place-name.
Same place-name error in the literal field: 宣德州 is Xuande Prefecture, not Xuanede.

decisions.after: He answered, "A ruler or father, in instructing his ministers or sons, likewise would not wish them to fall into unrighteousness.
decisions.reason: 君父教臣子 pairs ruler/father with ministers/sons. The revision restores the political and familial parallel without the awkward suggestion that one person is simultaneously both lord and father.
系楚材 means he was bound/fettered; the next unit 不肯解縛 confirms binding, so 'imprisoned' overstates the Chinese.

decisions.after: The emperor loved wine and drank daily with his ministers; Chucai remonstrated repeatedly in vain, then brought a wine trough with an iron spout and said, "Ferment can corrode things; if even iron is like this, how much more the five organs!"
decisions.reason: 曲蘗能腐物，鐵尚如此，況五臟乎 is an a fortiori from the corroded iron to the viscera. 'Ferment' is more historically precise than 'yeast,' and the revision preserves the argument's progression.

decisions.after: In the second year of Zhongtong he was posthumously given the title Duke Zhongsu.
decisions.reason: 追諡曰忠肅公 grants a posthumous title, not a temple name. The revision avoids the awkward phrase 'posthumous name Duke Zhongsu.'

decisions.after: Earlier, when Kublai campaigned against Song at Bian, Nanhe said, "Li Tan has received great favor from the state and holds a region on his own, yet he is deeply deceitful—rebellion is only a matter of time."
decisions.reason: 其人多詐 predicates deceit of Li Tan himself, not of his followers. The revision states that naturally rather than using the stilted phrase 'the man is full of deceit.'

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0014 shows English 'Xian' for 鉉 came only from the bad translation; the given-name claim must read Xuan while keeping zh, pinyin, id, subject, predicate, certainty, and evidence.
